title: Debriefing
subtitle: Things have settled down, but we still have business to take care of.

items.text: Debriefing
The sound of gunshots eventually draw in a set of footsteps.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Lilya! Aleksei! Hassan! Is that you?
Bertolt's voice echoes through the cave.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Bertolt!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: He followed my voice and quickly found the room, much easier than we did.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: The sight of Hassan lying next to Aleksei shocked him.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Hassan's courageous sacrifice will forever be remembered. He fought bravely against the enemy and died a hero.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Aleksei could not accept Bertolt's portrayal of what had happened.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: He was too principled for that.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: No, Commander. It was I who killed our comrade.
Lilya pulls out a bloodstained stack from under Hassan's body and throws it at Bertolt.
The thick files hit the ground, kicking up a swirl of dust around his army boots.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Congratulations, Commander. Mission complete.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: You went in earlier than I did, but you came out later.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: They wouldn't let me go.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Well, it seems you had a pleasant chat. Personally, I hate being questioned.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I'm an honest person.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Just like Aleksei.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: It's over now. Don't forget about your debriefing report.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Well done, my little falcon. You have survived Juhalerat. Your service on the battlefield is over for now, so you're free to return wherever you please.
Lilya does not reply. She looks back at the interrogation room, where the doors are now shut.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: How are you feeling about all this?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Not how I thought I would feel.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Of course, of course. For those who have never experienced war ...

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: War is often romanticized as a beautiful, idyllic symphony.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Until you're staring down the barrel of a gun, being mocked for your naivete.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: And you become just another tally, a statistic on the government's ledger.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hassan ...

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Zeno will take care of his wife, you can be sure of that.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Was this all "worth" it, Commander Bertolt?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: He was a joyful man. I cannot deny that we became good friends during our time together.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: The truth is, Hassan will serve as excellent promotional material. He'll become a true model.
So utilitarian, interest-oriented, and calculating.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Work for Zeno, earn your merits, and your family will be treated well.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: And for them, family and blood are above all else.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Two critters with one stone.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Let's go see Aleksei.
They walk to the interrogation room and peer at the silent young man through the window.
He notices the people outside, looks up, and halts his signing.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: He sees us. Aleksei is smiling.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I told you, this really isn't that big of a deal. It's just that he insisted on making this report himself.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Have you ever met someone who'd openly confess, "I am the one who shot our fellow comrade"?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I had no intention of sending him to a tribunal, but he was hell-bent on the notion.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: *sigh* Such a stubborn young man.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Having principles isn't easy.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: He didn't belong there. Juhalerat was not the right place for someone like him.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Or perhaps I should say he was not the right kind of person for a place like Juhalerat.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Semantics.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Don't worry about Aleksei. A young man like him will no doubt earn the admiral's favor.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: And this case will end up on the admiral's desk, I promise.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: As for you ...

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Your flight leaves tomorrow morning. The luggage in your room is already packed.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: How nice of you to do that.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Because you're going to take this story back to the academy.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: You will walk off the plane with coffins topped with black tulips.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: And you will tell your bratty little classmates ...

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: That perhaps one day, we might all end up in a black metal box.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: The front line still needs me, so this is it. I hope we'll have the chance to meet again, comrade.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Best of luck to you, Commander.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I almost forgot. I've got something for you. Aleksei left it with me before you got here.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: This. It was Hassan's.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text:
ZENO
A-150756
The officer cradles the name tag in his palm.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I don't remember making this for him. "ZENO" ... The tags of auxiliary forces should not have these letters engraved on them.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Aleksei told me he and Hassan got it secretly engraved last month.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hassan had always hoped to become a real part of Zeno. He loved being a part of this "big family."
Bertolt lowers his head in thought.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: He will have a real one made. I will fight to have his name inscribed in the Hall of Merit at our headquarters.
That dark and glorious corridor, lined with the names of those who died in battle and during the "Storm."

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: He will rest in the Zeno Cemetery as a true soldier of Zeno, with a dog tag bearing his name.
The officer turns and walks away, holding the keepsake tightly in his hand.
The sound of a soldier's boots echoes down the hall. Lilya takes one last glance at the room where her comrade had seemed so relieved.
Inside, Aleksei eagerly awaits his fate, while Zeno eagerly awaits him.
THE END
